substitutes: No pumpkin? Use a little more banana.
No baking paper? A silicone baking mat works.
title: The Little Dog Bakery
clue: A tray of tiny things, a hand-lettered sign and exactly one customer.
reveal: Bake a tiny batch of soft banana-pumpkin bites from three plain ingredients, then open your bakery for its one and only customer. Give the batch a name, make a menu board and let the Chief Taste Tester sample a single crumb.
objective: Bake a small batch of simple dog-safe bites, name them and open a pretend bakery for your dog.
instructions: Check the ingredients first: a ripe banana, plain 100% pumpkin puree (never pie filling), and plain oats cooked in water and cooled. Nothing else goes in: no sugar, salt, spice, peanut butter or milk.
Heat the oven to 175C/350F and line a tray with baking paper. Mash half a banana, then stir in one tablespoon of pumpkin and two tablespoons of the cooled cooked oats until sticky.

Dot the mix onto the tray in small drops, pea-sized for little dogs and thumbnail-sized for bigger ones. Bake about 15 minutes until set, then cool completely. Keep the dog out of the kitchen while the oven is hot.
While they cool, make the shop: a paper sign with your bakery's name, a menu board with your bite's name, and a cloth over a low table or tray. Your dog may supervise from their bed.
Open for business. Offer one cooled bite at your dog's own pace, with a little fuss about the 'order'. Whether they eat it, sniff it or wander off, the customer has spoken.
Count what you gave as part of today's treat allowance. Keep the rest in a covered container in the fridge for two days or freeze it, and write the recipe on a card to keep.
twist: You really bake, but the whole bakery serves one customer who gets a single bite, and the real product is the sign, the name and the recipe card.
variations: No-oven version: mash banana with a spoonful of pumpkin and serve a teaspoon from a clean saucer.
No-food version: bake nothing and run a 'Toy Bakery' where your dog picks a favorite toy from three on the counter.
For dogs on special or prescription diets: skip the recipe and plate a small portion of their regular food as the house special.
For small dogs or puppies: make drops pea-sized and offer half a bite.
completion: The batch is baked or skipped, the shop has opened and your dog has had the chance to sample, ignore or enjoy the one bite.
photoIdea: Your dog beside the shop sign with the cooling tray in the background, taken from their level.
memoryPrompt: What did you name your signature bite, and what did the Chief Taste Tester decide?
dietNotes: Only the dog-safe foods named here, counted in the day's allowance. No xylitol, chocolate, grapes, raisins, onion, garlic, macadamia. Allergy or prescription diet: use the no-food version.
safety: Never use xylitol, chocolate, raisins, grapes, onion, garlic or macadamia nuts. Ask your vet about your dog's diet.
Cool fully before serving, and keep the oven and hot tray out of your dog's reach.
Bites are soft but crumbly: cut small for little dogs and watch while they eat.
